name: Zaccur
overview: Zaccur was a male figure noted in the biblical record for his role in the restoration of Jerusalem's walls. His significant contribution was the rebuilding of a section of the wall, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:2. There is no mention of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this work.
namesAndTitles: The name Zaccur means "remembering" in Hebrew. It is a proper name and is not indicated to have been given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a personal or family heritage, but Scripture does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Zaccur is identified explicitly as the son of Imri, according to Nehemiah 3:2. Beyond this relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Zaccur's significance lies in his active participation in the physical and spiritual restoration of Jerusalem following the exile. By rebuilding part of the city wall, he contributed to the community's security and the fulfillment of God's promise to restore His people. His role exemplifies faithful service in the collective effort to rebuild both the city and the faith community under God's providence.
